Valley of Achor
AY-kor
proper noun (place)
Hebrew Achor, "trouble"; the valley where Achan was judged, which God promised to make "a door of hope."

📖 Biblical Definition

The valley of Achor, whose name means "trouble," was the place where Achan and his household were stoned after his sin had brought defeat upon Israel at Ai. Achan had taken of the accursed thing from Jericho, and for his hidden theft the army was routed; when the sin was uncovered, Joshua said, "Why hast thou troubled us? the LORD shall trouble thee this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones... Wherefore the name of that place was called, The valley of Achor, unto this day" (Josh 7:25-26). It was a place of judgment, where sin in the camp was purged. Yet the prophets transformed its meaning into one of the Bible's most beautiful promises of grace. Through Hosea the LORD pledged to His wayward people, "I will give her... the valley of Achor for a door of hope" (Hos 2:15), and Isaiah foresaw it as a resting-place for the flock (Isa 65:10). The valley of trouble would become a doorway into hope. Achor stands in the dictionary as the place where trouble is turned to hope, a witness that sin must be judged, yet that the God of grace can make the very valley of our trouble — rightly judged and repented of — the door through which we enter into renewed fellowship and hope.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The valley ("trouble") where Achan was judged for his sin (Josh 7:24-26), which God promised through Hosea to make "a door of hope" (Hos 2:15); a witness that sin must be judged, yet trouble can become a doorway into hope.

VALLEY OF ACHOR, proper noun. "Trouble"; where Achan was judged (Josh 7:24-26).

The place where sin in the camp was purged after the defeat at Ai.

"Why hast thou troubled us? the LORD shall trouble thee this day" (Josh 7:25).

Promised by God as "a door of hope" (Hos 2:15).

Foreseen by Isaiah as a resting-place for the flock (Isa 65:10).

📖 Key Scripture

Josh 7:25 — "And Joshua said, Why hast thou troubled us? the LORD shall trouble thee this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones."

Josh 7:26 — "...Wherefore the name of that place was called, The valley of Achor, unto this day."

Hos 2:15 — "And I will give her her vineyards from thence, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope: and she shall sing there, as in the days of her youth..."

Isa 65:10 — "And Sharon shall be a fold of flocks, and the valley of Achor a place for the herds to lie down in, for my people that have sought me."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Achor needs no defense from redefinition; its lessons are that sin in the camp must be judged, and that the God of grace can turn the valley of trouble into a door of hope for the repentant.

expand to see more

Sin-tolerated correction. Israel could not stand before its enemies while the accursed thing was hidden in the camp. The valley of Achor teaches that hidden sin brings defeat, and must be uncovered and judged before blessing returns. The dictionary holds the seriousness of sin in the church: it cannot be tolerated or concealed without cost, and the path to renewed strength runs through honest confession and the purging of evil from among the people of God.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the gospel turn from trouble to hope. The God who judged sin at Achor promised to make that very valley "a door of hope" (Hos 2:15). The dictionary commends this grace: when sin is judged and repented of, God can transform the place of our deepest trouble into the doorway of renewed fellowship and song, so that the valley named for trouble becomes the threshold of hope for those who seek Him.
